precepts.text: So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite's hope shall perish: whose hope shall be cut off, and whose trust shall be a spider's web. He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand. Get tangled in that web and the spider comes out to eat you; a house built on it will not endure.
precepts.point: The way of peace they know not; and there is no judgment in their goings: they have made them crooked paths; whosoever goeth therein shall not know peace. You follow the Democratic or the Republican party, you follow the cross and the idols, you are not going to find peace. Our people have made crooked paths for themselves.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
Isaiah 59 says they “weave the spider’s web” and “Their webs shall not become garments”. Job explains the spider's web. “So are the paths of all that forget God; and the hypocrite’s hope shall perish: Whose hope shall be cut off”, because they are hypocrites, “and whose trust shall be a spider’s web.”

Their trust shall be as a spider's web: you get tangled up in that thing, and that spider comes out and bites you and eats you up.

“He shall lean upon his house, but it shall not stand: he shall hold it fast, but it shall not endure.” Your house won't stand. A people who forget God weave their webs and lean on what they built, but it cannot cover them or hold them up. That is why Isaiah 59:6 goes on, “neither shall they cover themselves with their works: their works are works of iniquity, and the act of violence is in their hands.”

precepts.text: Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors: when you learn from their examples, it gives us a guide for today. That is called legacy.
precepts.point: They ignorantly call themselves young ones in the streets, and this generation culture is not your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings? When we bethink, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

precepts.why:
Isaiah 51:20 says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. What other people on the planet are at the head of every corner on the streets? That's us: in Miami, in the Bronx, in all the hoods and all the ghettos throughout the whole earth. We fainted, we are hid in prison houses, and we are on every corner. They ignorantly call us YNs, and we call ourselves YNs, uncs and OGs, but that ain't your culture. Whatever happened to the ancients, the hoary head, the elders of our nation, the kings?

So the Lord says, “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Prepare yourself for the search of your ancestors. When we bethink ourselves, we come back to our heritage and to knowing who we are. It is no longer, I'm a YN: we have young prophets amongst us. We are raising up our sons and daughters, young men, teens and young adults, in the understanding that they are the children of the prophets, the sons and daughters of God.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” What our fathers went through was written for our learning, to increase our faith. When you learn from the examples of our ancestors, it gives us a guide for how we need to be today. That's called legacy.

How did our ancestors handle famine, persecution and tribulation? Job lost his children and his wealth and was covered in boils, and he said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord hath taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.” Abraham was called to go out and “went out, not knowing whither he went”, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. We are going to have to get back to that, and who else did it but us? We are them; they are us.

precepts.text: Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers; looking up the history is a command, not a fixation.
precepts.point: Unto thee it was shewed, that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Looking up the history is a command, not a fixation.

Moses says the same: “ask now of the days that are past, which were before thee, since the day that God created man upon the earth”. You are supposed to search out your forefathers and look up your history, and not slavery only: the reign under David and Solomon and the empires where Israel ruled, and slavery too, because failing to keep the laws is why the people went into it.

Search it and there is no such history anywhere else. No other people heard the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire and lived; no other nation was taken from the midst of another nation “by temptations, by signs, and by wonders, and by war, and by a mighty hand”. The Most High did this for Israel alone, “that thou mightest know that the Lord he is God; there is none else beside him.”

precepts.text: Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers.
precepts.point: Paul advised the churches the same way his forefather Moses did: the things written aforetime, the Torah itself, were written for our learning. In Romans he quotes Moses over and over, including from this very chapter.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Remember the days of old, consider the years of many generations: ask thy father, and he will shew thee; thy elders, and they will tell thee.” Job says the same: “For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Study who we were, see where our fathers went wrong, and do not do the same thing.

Before you learned this truth, did you know who you were before 1619? Did you know the many generations of your forefathers? Somebody had to show you. When we suffer persecution and trials we can go to the scriptures and see how the Most High intervened and saved our forefathers. That is how you are supposed to read this Bible, like you stepped into the events themselves: enquiring of the former age, searching out the fathers.

precepts.text: Enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers; we are supposed to know these things so nobody can pull the wool over our eyes.
precepts.point: This is why we must know our history. The king of Ammon could have pulled that on somebody ignorant and been given the land; Jephthah said no, that is not what happened, the book of Numbers does not say that. People try to confuse us about the Bible in the street the same way, so prepare yourself to the search of the fathers.

note.label: Judges 11: Jephthah and the Search of the Fathers

precepts.why:
“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Jephthah knew the record: “Israel took not away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon”. He broke down the whole history to the king of Ammon, so nobody could talk him out of it. The king could have pulled that on somebody ignorant and been given the land; Jephthah said no, that is not what happened, the book of Numbers does not say that.

This is why we must know our history. People try to confuse us about the Bible in the street the same way, so prepare yourself to the search of the fathers; we are supposed to know these things so nobody can pull the wool over our eyes.

precepts.text: Inquire of the former age and prepare thyself to the search of thy fathers, for it matters whose son you are.
precepts.point: The nations call us a minority and divide us by many labels so they can deal wisely with us, but we are not a minority, and the Most High promised to multiply our seed like the stars of heaven and the sand of the sea.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 2: The Sons of Israel and the Line of Judah

precepts.why:
“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. It matters whose son you are.

That is why the record sets down “the sons of Israel” by name. When we search out our fathers, we find these twelve, and we carry their name, their lineage and their descent.

precepts.text: Enquire of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers.
precepts.point: This is the same lesson for our people today. We are going through days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord. Search out the former age and the fathers, for this is the story of our people, and it is history to lean on in our own affliction.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
“For Almighty God hath turned to joy unto them the day, wherein the chosen people should have perished.” That is why this is written down and kept: it is the story of our people, and it is history to lean on in our own affliction.

“For enquire, I pray thee, of the former age, and prepare thyself to the search of their fathers”. Search out the former age and the fathers. What the Most High did for Israel in Persia, turning the day of death into a day of joy, is what he does. We are going through days of sorrow, but joy is coming as long as we stay in the commandments and trust in the Lord. Esther's day is the former age we enquire of to know that.

precepts.text: Bildad said if your children sinned against God, He is going to take them away; their sin was celebrating their birthdays, which is not a custom of Israel.
precepts.point: Job sanctified them and rose up early to offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, for Job said it may be that his sons had sinned and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.

note.label: Job 1: The Trial of an Upright Man

precepts.why:
Bildad said, “If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression”. If your children sinned against God, he is going to take them away. And their sin was celebrating their birthdays, which is not a custom of Israel.

That is what “every one his day” means in Job 1:4: his sons went and feasted in their houses, every one his day, and they were talking about their birthdays. Whenever somebody's birthday came around they would say, this is my day, this is my day. Now people have gotten to the point where it is, this is my month, my birthday month, so I am celebrating the whole month. Same thing with this.

Job knew it. When the days of their feasting were gone about, he sanctified them and rose up early to offer burnt offerings according to the number of them all, “for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts.” Thus did Job continually.

precepts.text: Job was perfect and upright, one that feared God and eschewed evil, contradicting Bildad's assumption.
precepts.point: Though his beginning was small, his latter end should greatly increase. Bildad promises restoration, but on the false premise that Job is not already upright.

note.label: Job 8: Bildad Argues the Most High Does Not Pervert Judgment

precepts.why:
Bildad says, “If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee”. But the book already told us: “There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.”

Job was perfect and upright, one that feared God and eschewed evil, which contradicts Bildad's assumption. Bildad promises restoration, that though his beginning was small his latter end should greatly increase, but on the false premise that Job is not already upright.

precepts.text: Job offered burnt offerings for his ten children in case they had sinned and cursed God in their hearts.
precepts.point: Though his beginning was small, his latter end should greatly increase. Bildad promises restoration, but on the false premise that Job is not already upright.

note.label: Job 8: Bildad Argues the Most High Does Not Pervert Judgment

precepts.why:
Bildad tells Job, “If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty”. Job already did: “Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.”

Job rose up early and offered burnt offerings for his ten children in case they had sinned and cursed God in their hearts, and he did it continually. He was seeking God betimes before Bildad ever told him to. Bildad's promise rests on the false premise that Job is not already upright.

precepts.text: God will not cast away a perfect man; they that hate thee shall be clothed with shame and the dwelling place of the wicked come to nought.
precepts.point: The evildoers hate the light and love darkness. But upon Christ his crown, his rulership, will flourish forever, because he has budded as a leader and his second coming will flourish forevermore.

note.label: Psalm 132: The Oath to David and the Throne Forever

precepts.why:
“His enemies will I clothe with shame: but upon himself shall his crown flourish.” “Behold, God will not cast away a perfect man, neither will he help the evil doers: Till he fill thy mouth with laughing, and thy lips with rejoicing. They that hate thee shall be clothed with shame; and the dwelling place of the wicked shall come to nought.”

The enemies clothed with shame are not only the nations but the wickedness of our own people, the evildoers, who will be clothed in shame when the day of judgment comes. The evildoers hate the light and love darkness. But upon Christ his crown, his rulership, will flourish for ever, because he has budded as a leader and his second coming will flourish for evermore.

points: Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase. I joined in 2006; IUIC was not the most revered school, and the early YouTube page was not the grandest. Others covering conspiracies got far more views, but the content here changed my life: I understood this is what we need as a people. Look at us now; look at where this body has grown, because there were people that understood what was necessary for the nation. It took true vision and true dedication, and we did it together. This is not a one man show.

The booster club is genius: they wonder how we put boots on the ground all over the world. It is because we come together with the same mind. Though I cannot be there physically, here is some money so you all can get over there and make it happen.

Video played, the bishops on what makes this body different: at Israel United in Christ we are sincere about bringing the truth to the people; there is no ulterior motive to take advantage of people, and there is a sincere love for our people. Our people need the medicine that the Most High has in that Bible, and we need it too, so there is no room for trying to get over on our people or on each other. Other congregations have simply given up the fight and do not want anyone to show them up; that is where the hatred comes from.

Video continued: what separated this school was going into the law with precepts, not pushing things that are not there: not a six pointed star, not that you must learn Hebrew to be saved. Meanwhile our people are on drugs, killing each other; husbands do not know how to be husbands, wives do not know how to be wives, and the kids are out of order. The focus here was on the family, instilling morals, principles, and values, teaching men how to be brothers and how to be friends. When the Most High cast us out of his sight, we knew Hebrew and we knew who we were; the problem was that we were ungodly, so first we take responsibility for our actions, repent, and keep the law.

The separation was made long ago, and it was not us that did it; the Lord did it. We are just the ones that decided to do what he said. When the Lord said be ye separate, it means just that: this body is too important to be affiliated with any nonsense.
